## Context / Problem
`tests/unit/test_mcp_idle_heap_release.py::test_finished_background_job_does_not_keep_its_memory` fails on every `sweep (py3.14t)` run since it landed in 9beecb409ab: 13 of 13 runs from 43991050364 (2026-11-17) through 44390588952 (2026-11-18), always this one test, always 271-275 MiB kept (e.g. job 135106845268: baseline 2224 MiB, before release 2499 MiB, idle +272 MiB). The `sweep (py3.14)` leg on the same ubuntu runner and glibc passes in the same runs. It is deterministic, not flaky.

Root cause: the test's premise is glibc-arena behaviour. Its large `str` objects are allocated through `PyObject_Malloc`. In a GIL build that goes to glibc `malloc` for objects over 512 bytes, so `malloc_trim(0)` (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py::release_freed_heap`) returns the freed pages. In the free-threaded build CPython routes `PyObject_Malloc` and `PyMem_Malloc` through its bundled mimalloc, which is required and cannot be disabled there (CPython 3.14 C-API docs, "Memory Management": default allocators table, and "The mimalloc allocator"). glibc `malloc_trim` cannot release mimalloc segments, so the freed ~274 MiB stays resident: the trim is a no-op for exactly the memory the test measures. The deployed MCP image is `python:3.12-slim` (GIL build, `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp`), so the production release path is unaffected; `sweep (py3.14t)` is an experimental, nonblocking leg.

## Approach
Scope the memory test to the builds whose object memory glibc owns: skip it when `sysconfig.get_config_var("Py_GIL_DISABLED")` is truthy, with a reason naming mimalloc. Add one sentence to `release_freed_heap`'s docstring stating that on free-threaded builds Python objects live in mimalloc, which `malloc_trim` does not govern. No change to the release mechanism itself: there is no public CPython API to collect mimalloc heaps, and no deployed image runs free-threaded. No config key, env var or flag.

Rejected: retrying or loosening the 64 MiB threshold (the retained amount equals the whole freed amount, so any threshold that passes would make the test meaningless); calling private mimalloc symbols through ctypes (unexported, version-fragile).

Portability: test-only skip condition using `sysconfig`, available on every platform and interpreter; no subprocesses, fds, paths or signals.

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_idle_heap_release.py` — add the free-threaded skip to the memory test.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` — docstring sentence on `release_freed_heap` only.

## Testing
- GIL builds: the memory test still runs and passes on the Linux CI cells (ubuntu py3.11-3.13) and `sweep (py3.14)`; macOS and Windows still skip it as before.
- Free-threaded build: after merge, dispatch `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main`; in `sweep (py3.14t)` this test no longer fails (it is skipped with the mimalloc reason). Any other failure in that job is unrelated and gets its own ticket.
- `make verify` green in the worktree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Root cause identified with evidence (deterministic on free-threaded builds vs intermittent).
- [x] On the post-merge `sweep (py3.14t)` job the memory test no longer fails: it is skipped on the free-threaded build with a reason naming mimalloc, and it still runs on the GIL `sweep (py3.14)` leg. No retry-until-green and no loosened threshold.
- [x] `make verify` passes and the change lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
